title: RNA Extraction from Frozen Brain Tissue Using a Bullet Blender
author: Ashley V Kumar
materials: Begin by resuspending the tissue sample in 500 µL of chilled TRIzol‱ Reagent. Transfer the mixture to a Safe-Lock tube, ensuring that the sample remains cold throughout handling. Add 10 µL of RNase-free Zirconium Beads (0.5 mm; Cat. no. ZrOB05-RNA) to the tube. Perform all steps on ice.

steps.title: Homogenize Tissue
steps.instruction: Process prepared Safe-Lock tubes in the Bullet Blender to homogenize tissue.

substeps.instruction: Process at speed 6 for 1 minute in a cold room.
Inspect samples; if tissue remains unhomogenized, repeat processing only for those specific samples.

steps.title: Collect Supernatant
steps.instruction: Recover the TRIzol Reagent from the tubes.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 rpm for 30 seconds at 4°C.
Carefully transfer the supernatant to a new RNase-free tube kept on ice.

steps.title: Adjust TRIzol Volume
steps.instruction: Increase the volume of TRIzol Reagent in the supernatant tube.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of chilled TRIzol Reagent to the tube to bring the final volume to 1 mL.
Mix gently to ensure the sample is fully suspended.

steps.title: Perform Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the RNA from proteins and DNA using chloroform or TET buffer under a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent used for lysis (or add 0.2 mL of TET buffer [0.05% Tween, 1 mM EDTA, 10 mM Tris, pH 7.5] if using TRIzol LS).
Immediately cap the tube securely.
Incubate for 2–3 minutes at room temperature.
Briefly vortex for 3–5 seconds until the mixture appears homogeneous.

steps.title: Centrifuge for Layer Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the mixture into three distinct layers.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C using a swinging bucket rotor.

steps.title: Transfer Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Isolate the RNA-containing aqueous phase under a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.5 µL of RNase-free GlycoBlue Coprecipitant to a new, labeled tube while the previous centrifugation is in progress.
Tilt the tube at a 45° angle and gently pipette the upper colorless aqueous phase into the tube containing GlycoBlue.
If contamination from lower layers is risked, perform a quick re-spin before transferring.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Precipitate the RNA using sodium acetate and isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 1/10th volume of 3M sodium acetate (NaOAc) to the aqueous phase.
Mix by briefly vortexing and spin down the tube.
Add 1 volume of 100% isopropanol and vortex well.
Incubate for 20 minutes on ice, or alternatively, overnight at -20°C (do not use -80°C).

steps.title: Pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Concentrate the precipitated RNA into a pellet.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 28,000 × g (maximum speed) for 30 minutes at 4°C using a fixed-angle rotor.
Discard the supernatant with a micropipette, taking care not to disturb the pellet.
Perform a quick spin and remove any leftover liquid.

steps.title: Wash RNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet to remove residual contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent used.
Gently invert the tube to ensure the ethanol contacts the pellet.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 1–2 minutes at 4°C (or perform a quick spin).
Discard supernatant with a micropipette; perform a quick spin and use a P20 pipette to remove remaining ethanol at room temperature.

steps.title: Dry and Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Dry the pellet and resuspend the RNA.

substeps.instruction: Air dry the pellet at room temperature for 5 minutes, or until the shiny appearance is gone.
Add 12 µL of RNase-free water or TET (adjust volume for desired concentration).
Incubate at 55–60°C for 2 minutes, then immediately place on ice.
